display.title: Chai Elul: The Birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains Chai Elul, the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, and their main lesson: serve Hashem with joy.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that Chai Elul, the 18th of Elul, is a happy day for the Jewish people: it is the birthday of two great souls, the Baal Shem Tov, born in 1698, and the Alter Rebbe, born 47 years later in 1745. Every year on Chai Elul we gather to learn their teachings and make good resolutions about behavior, respect for parents and elders, davening and Torah study, and we pray that their merit protects us and opens new channels of blessing. One of their main lessons is to serve Hashem with joy, as Dovid HaMelech writes in Tehillim, 'Ivdu es Hashem b'simcha'. This is especially true in Elul, when, as the Alter Rebbe writes in Likkutei Torah, Hashem shows everyone a happy, radiant face, so we answer with joy of our own.
display.lesson: Celebrate Chai Elul with good resolutions, and serve Hashem with joy.
